slides.headline: MOST NEWSLETTERS BLEED SUBSCRIBERS BECAUSE THEY SOUND LIKE ADS AND THESE 6 CLAUDE PROMPTS FIX THAT FREE.
slides.image_prompt: Dario Amodei mid-toss, arms wide, joyful, shirtsleeves rolled. Envelopes exploding upward in mail-room. Claude logo glowing burnt-orange neon. Documentary news photo, 35mm, harsh flash, warm amber, tangerine-charcoal.

slides.headline: 1) WRITE THE SUBJECT LINE THAT ACTUALLY GETS OPENED
slides.body: Email copywriters charge $150 an hour for subject lines that hit average open rates. This prompt gives you 10 scored variations in under 60 seconds.

slides.headline: 2) WRITE THE FULL NEWSLETTER BODY IN YOUR OWN VOICE
slides.body: Newsletter writers take two full days per issue and charge hourly for every revision. Most business owners spend four hours writing what this prompt writes in three minutes.

slides.headline: 3) WRITE THE PS LINE THAT DRIVES ALL YOUR CLICKS
slides.body: The PS is the second-most-read section of any email, right after the subject line. Most link clicks in a newsletter come from the PS, and almost nobody writes it on purpose.

slides.headline: 4) BUILD THE 3-EMAIL WELCOME SEQUENCE NEW SUBSCRIBERS GET
slides.body: New subscribers are 3 times more likely to buy in their first 48 hours than after 30 days. Most businesses send one welcome email and waste the entire window.

slides.headline: 5) WIN BACK THE SUBSCRIBERS WHO STOPPED OPENING
slides.body: The average email list loses 25% of its engaged readers every year. One re-engagement campaign can recover 15 to 20% of them without spending anything on new leads.

slides.headline: 6) SELL IN YOUR NEWSLETTER WITHOUT SOUNDING LIKE AN AD
slides.body: Most promotional emails fail because they read like ads. An email copywriter charges $1,000 to $3,000 to write one that reads like a story and still closes.

slides.headline: SAVE THIS
slides.body: You will want these when your next newsletter is due. Every prompt pastes straight into Claude and works in under four minutes. Daily AI news and real skills at @yaffeai

caption:
